**Course source:** Day 3 §2. The running application contains Product, Order and User services.

## Why Zuul appears after Nginx

The historical course introduces Netflix **Zuul** as a gateway integrated with Spring Cloud discovery and filters. Rather than configuring every target address directly in an Nginx file, the gateway can route to a logical service known to the registry.

~~~text
Client -> Zuul route /api/order/** -> discovered Order instance
                      |
                  pre / route / post / error filters
~~~

The exact filter categories and execution model belong to the Zuul generation in the uploaded material. They are valuable for understanding a gateway **pipeline**, even when a newer gateway uses different APIs.

## Filters have distinct responsibilities

A **pre-routing filter** might attach a correlation ID or validate required credentials. A **routing filter** chooses the upstream and forwards the request. A **post-routing filter** can add response headers or record measurements. Error handling should turn upstream failures into a clear client contract.

Do not trust a request header claiming to be an administrator merely because it arrived at the gateway. Authentication must validate credentials, and downstream business operations still need authorisation.

## Failure scenario

Suppose Product is unavailable but Order remains up. A gateway should not mark the entire shop unavailable solely because one route fails. It can return a route-specific 502 or 503, depending on the failure and policy.

## How to read the old source code

Follow one request from route match, through filter ordering, to selected upstream and final response. The course's source walkthrough explains an implementation of this path. Avoid transplanting historical filter classes directly into a new Spring project.

## Current direction

For modern Spring Cloud deployments, investigate **Spring Cloud Gateway** and compare it against ingress gateways and reverse proxies already provided by the platform.

[Spring Cloud Gateway documentation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-cloud-gateway/reference/).

## Check your understanding

Explain the request or event path end to end. Which component can fail, and which information would you collect to diagnose that failure?
